title: Announcements / Send learning materials or send to Canvas → Shareable link
intro: Internal board for the Essentials 2.0 solution concept (Semester → Courses → Announcements / send materials → Shareable link). Not about UI: each reference shows how another product lets someone running a course communicate from inside it: announce to everyone or a group, send selected files or links ahead of a session, choose the channel (portal feed, email, shareable link, Canvas LMS), schedule it, and see who received or opened it. One section per question; every card says what we would take from it. Counter-examples are flagged. Raw material from Mobbin and Refero, to be cut down in the converge pass before anything is shown outside the team.

questions.title: Composer: audience targeting (course / group / individual), attachment of course materials, scheduling
questions.answer: Every composer in the set treats scheduling as a property of the send action, not a separate feature: Slack's send-button dropdown with presets and a custom date/time (mobbin:fd356e91), Whop's inline calendar popover (mobbin:16eb85ed), LinkedIn's clock icon (refero:863), Basecamp's 'Schedule and save' (mobbin:25c42c82). Audience targeting is rarer and coarser than the question assumes: Google Classroom puts a 'For / All students' dropdown directly above the text box (refero:19605564), Teachable offers everyone / a course / an individual (refero:9617), The Leap uses described segments (refero:4564), and Confluence only Public/Private plus a start–end window (mobbin:fcc604e7). Attachments are inline uploads (ClassDojo photo, Basecamp PDF, Whop image); nobody attaches from a course library. Only The Leap closes the loop from recipients through confirmation to open/click stats. Confluence's one-active-banner cap is the caveat: a persistent materials banner and a timely one cannot coexist.

questions.title: Channel choice (in-app feed, email, push, link, external LMS) and whether it is one composer or many features
questions.answer: Two models. 'One composer, many channels' puts the channel as a control on the same post: beehiiv's Post / Email / Website / Delivery tabs reconcile into a per-channel recipient summary before sending (mobbin:748e794e); Kit layers a 'Publish to web' opt-in over a default email send (mobbin:f722d4bb); Intercom folds platform (web / iOS / Android) and push into one panel (mobbin:7380bc5c). 'Implicit channel' treats the in-app post as the channel and only asks who is notified: Basecamp separates 'who should see this' from 'when I post this, notify…' (mobbin:0bc24c79), and Substack bundles email and push into a single default-on 'notify subscribers' toggle (mobbin:a7ebc4ec). Nobody in the set exposes an external LMS as a channel inside the composer; that lives in an export menu (see Q5). The useful distinction for a course is visibility versus notification: the post is the record, the channels are how people hear about it.

questions.title: Shareable link controls (expiry, access level, revoke, tracking)
questions.answer: Link controls converge on one panel with five questions: who can open (anyone / workspace / specific people), at what level (view / comment / edit), until when, with which password, and how to revoke. Mural shows all five, including a timezone-stamped expiry and a 'Reset visitor link' that regenerates rather than merely disables (mobbin:836e980f); Proton has expiry, password and 'Stop sharing' (mobbin:ef4fcd7f); Notion resolves relative presets ('in a week') to an absolute date inline and ends with a red Remove (mobbin:cfca14fb). Coda (mobbin:c333ff8e), Dropbox (mobbin:777c4ef0) and Sketch (mobbin:1fb17c11) focus on tiered access (workspace / guests / everyone) and per-person levels, with Copy link always in the same corner; Sketch splits public rights into download versus comment checkboxes. Only Loom shows tracking next to the share ('No views yet', refero:1242). ClickUp is the counter-example (mobbin:7f248abd): expiry defaults to Never with no presets, no access level, and the only revoke is an all-or-nothing Unpublish.

questions.title: Delivery feedback (sent / delivered / seen, reminders)
questions.answer: Feedback is worth having only when it is per person and has an action next to it. Navan lists each invitee with a status, lets you select the non-responders and 'Send a reminder' from the same table (mobbin:9d8af34f); Superhuman shows per-person, per-device, timestamped opens inline on the thread itself (mobbin:ba56c2de). Automation goes further: HoneyBook branches the follow-up on 'file viewed within 1 day' (mobbin:8afb0d65); Docusign lets you set the days before the first reminder and the repeat interval (mobbin:e4a526c1). Newsletter tools lead with aggregate counters (Mailchimp mobbin:6db18da5, HubSpot mobbin:5814d24c; Dub for link clicks, refero:2fe44823) and keep per-recipient detail one tab away (Outseta's Recipients tab with last-opened timestamps, mobbin:34451b74). WhatsApp's Delivered / Read is the minimum: two states, one recipient (mobbin:5580e66f). Square's Announcements list is the caution (mobbin:1c8c3422): a 'Seen by' column that shows nothing and offers no follow-up action.

questions.title: External LMS hand-off UX (auth, mapping to course, what is sent, confirmation)
questions.answer: The thinnest question in the set and the most important one for Essentials. Only SchoolAI shows a complete hand-off (mobbin:3135010e): an Export menu that lists Google Classroom next to Docs / PDF, a permission modal that says what will be shared, an OAuth enable step, a Class picker that maps the document to one specific class, and an 'Exported to Google Classroom!' toast. Course platforms in the set have no hand-off at all: in Kajabi, publishing inside the product is the send, so the learner-facing surface is the product's own portal (mobbin:9aa981d2). Generic connectors stop at authorization: Craft is a Connect / Disconnect toggle on a settings page (mobbin:e9079303), and Cofounder's OAuth flow with per-scope toggles never reaches a 'what was sent' or success state (mobbin:7897406d, counter-example). Nobody shows editing or re-syncing after the hand-off.

questions.title: Learner-side reception (feed, notification, email) and consistency with the portal
questions.answer: The consistent products give announcements a distinct type or place on the learner side. Microsoft Teams offers 'Post' versus 'Announcement' in the composer and renders announcements with a bold title and replies attached (mobbin:88ad5199); Circle routes them to an 'Announcements' space separate from the feed (mobbin:c1b1c3ad); ClassDojo keeps a teacher-only Pin so the post stays on top, with the attachment and replies inline (mobbin:3edf67a5). Unread state is aggregated centrally in Slack's Activity screen rather than only inside the source channel (mobbin:8e65f9c9), and Spotify lets the recipient choose email versus push per category, a model for learner notification preferences (refero:471b8f0c). Coursera is the counter-example (mobbin:36db9592): instructor content sits in a 'Latest'-sorted Q&A list with no pin, no unread marker and no sender role, so an announcement is indistinguishable from peer chatter.

references.title: Message scheduling with date/time and audience notification options
references.question: Q1
references.take: PDF-attached message composer with a clock-icon schedule popover (date/time, 'Schedule and save'); no audience or notification controls on this screen.

references.title: Scheduling a post with file attachments flow
references.question: Q1
references.take: New Post modal for one class: attach a photo, optional AI writing assist, then a calendar-and-time scheduler; there is no audience selector because the class is the audience.

references.title: Creating an announcement flow
references.question: Q1
references.take: Admin announcement-banner flow: title, banner style, Public/Private audience radio and an optional start/end date-time window with timezone; only one banner can be active at a time.

references.title: Stream composer: "Announce to class" box with All students picker
references.question: Q1
references.take: The class Stream page pairs a lightweight "Announce something to your class" text box with a "For / All students" audience dropdown directly above it, showing that audience targeting can live as one control next to the compose field instead of a separate step.

references.title: LinkedIn: compose a post, then open a date/time scheduling dialog
references.question: Q1
references.take: LinkedIn's composer exposes a scheduling entry point in the compose toolbar that opens a dedicated date-and-time picker before the post is queued, showing how scheduling can be an optional side-dialog off the main composer rather than a separate screen or mode.

references.title: Scheduling a message flow
references.question: Q1
references.take: Scheduling lives on the send button: a dropdown of presets or a custom date/time modal with timezone; channel targeting and attachments are not exercised in these steps.

references.title: Teachable: compose and send a broadcast email to a recipient group
references.question: Q1
references.take: Announcement email composer with a Send-to dropdown (everyone / a course / an individual) plus subject and body, a confirm modal, then a sent state; no attachment is used.

references.title: The Leap: broadcast composer with template, editor, and recipient segments
references.question: Q1
references.take: The Leap's broadcast flow chains a template chooser into a rich-text editor with a dedicated recipients dropdown for picking one or more contact segments, then forces a review-and-confirm modal before send and finishes on a sent-state screen with immediate analytics — a model for pairing audience targeting with an explicit confirm step in a course composer.

references.title: Scheduling an announcement flow
references.question: Q1
references.take: Composer with an embedded image where an inline calendar popover switches the primary action between publish now and scheduled; no audience control.

references.title: Message with notification recipient and audience control
references.question: Q2
references.take: One message-board composer that separates 'Who should see this?' (team only vs allow client) from 'When I post this, notify…' (requester / everyone I select / no one); the in-app post is the channel.

references.title: Excluded segments and delivery options
references.question: Q2
references.take: Delivery tab of a single post object with Post / Email / Website / SEO tabs: segment exclusions, a web-access toggle and a per-channel recipient summary (Email: 6, Web: all free subscribers) before Schedule or Send.

references.title: Run a test with email collector and push notification options
references.question: Q2
references.take: Content tab of one message composer mixing reply type (chat vs email collector), platform (Web / iOS / Android) and a mobile push toggle in a single panel; audience routing is not on this screen.

references.title: Send list with audience and delivery channel selection
references.question: Q2
references.take: Single broadcast composer with an audience filter builder, a send-time field that defaults to 'Send now', and a 'Publish to web' toggle as an extra channel on top of the default email.

references.title: Publish with audience and delivery notification iOS
references.question: Q2
references.take: iOS publish modal showing audience (who can view), notification delivery toggle for email/push, and send controls.

references.title: Share link with expiration settings (iOS)
references.question: Q3
references.take: Public tab of the share sheet: public link, 'Expire link after: Never' with no presets, search-engine toggle, per-field visibility toggles, and Unpublish as the only, all-or-nothing revoke.

references.title: Sharing a doc
references.question: Q3
references.take: Complete flow showing access mode selection (anyone, specific people), recipient selection, copy link action, and permission confirmation in a document sharing dialog.

references.title: Sharing a document
references.question: Q3
references.take: Share dialog with an 'Anyone with this link: can edit' dropdown, add-person-by-email with a note, and Copy link; expiration and password sit behind an unopened Settings link.

references.title: Loom: share dialog with per-person permission level and invited list
references.question: Q3
references.take: Loom's Share dialog lets the owner add a person or Space and set a permission level (e.g. Can view) before sending the invite, then confirms the person now appears in an invited/access list — a pattern for showing who currently has access to a shared item, not just generating a link.

references.title: Link sharing access and expiration settings
references.question: Q3
references.take: Access and settings panel showing restricted/general access options, visitor link access controls, expiration date, password, and reset visitor link button.

references.title: Link expiration and access controls (iOS)
references.question: Q3
references.take: iOS link access dialog showing access level options (can edit, can comment, can view), link expiration with time presets (1 hour, 1 day, 1 week), and remove access option.

references.title: Share link settings with expiration and password
references.question: Q3
references.take: Settings dialog for shared link with expiration date field, password requirement toggle, and stop sharing option to revoke access.

references.title: Share a document with permissions
references.question: Q3
references.take: Share dialog with three access tiers (Workspace members / Guests / Everyone); the public-link tier has a view-or-no-access radio plus separate Inspect-and-download and Comment checkboxes, Copy Link fixed top-right.

references.title: Turning on auto reminders with conditions
references.question: Q4
references.take: Advanced reminder setup: expiration date, recipient privileges, auto-reminder toggle, days before first reminder, repeat interval, and custom number of days config.

references.title: Dub link analytics: clicks/leads/sales for a tagged share link
references.question: Q4
references.take: Dub's Analytics view shows Clicks/Leads/Sales counters plus a time-series chart for links filtered by tag, evidence that link-level delivery feedback can be a few aggregate counters and a trend line rather than a per-recipient log of who clicked.

references.title: Adding conditions for automated reminders
references.question: Q4
references.take: Workflow showing automation setup: send email, wait for 1 day, check if file was viewed within that period, then branch to send different followup emails.

references.title: Email campaign recipient engagement metrics
references.question: Q4
references.take: Campaign Analyze tab with aggregate metrics only (Sent, Delivered rate, Open / Click / Reply rate, bounce, unsubscribe, spam); no per-recipient list or action on this screen.

references.title: Email campaign report with sent, opened, clicked counts
references.question: Q4
references.take: Campaign analytics overview showing 3 recipients, delivered, clicked, bounced, unsubscribed counts; recipient activity tab with open/click tracking per recipient.

references.title: Sending a reminder to non-responders
references.question: Q4
references.take: Flow showing invite creation, reminder selection from invite list, and confirmation to send reminder email to selected non-responders.

references.title: Newsletter performance metrics with opened/clicked tracking
references.question: Q4
references.take: Recipients tab of a sent broadcast: one row per recipient with Last opened / Clicked / Unsubscribed timestamps and status sub-filters (Opened, Clicked, Bounced…) plus Export; no resend action on this screen.

references.title: Announcement status - sent indicator
references.question: Q4
references.take: Announcements list with a Status column (Sent) and a separate 'Seen by' column that is empty for the row shown; the field exists without data and without a follow-up action.

references.title: Message read status indicators
references.question: Q4
references.take: Mail interface showing team read statuses with opened/unopened indicator: June and Perry have opened, and the view shows who has opened messages.

references.title: Message read and delivered status (iOS)
references.question: Q4
references.take: Per-message info screen with two states, Read and Delivered (timestamped); the minimum viable feedback, single recipient, no breakdown.

references.title: OAuth-based app connection workflow
references.question: Q5
references.take: OAuth connect flow for cross-posting: destination picker, per-scope permission toggles, a 'continue sharing?' re-consent screen, then a loading state; the flow ends before showing what was sent or any success state.

references.title: Connecting and integrating third-party services
references.question: Q5
references.take: Settings-page list of integrations (Figma, GitHub, Jira, Linear) with a bare Connect / Disconnect toggle; no destination, no content, no confirmation of anything sent.

references.title: Publishing course content to members
references.question: Q5
references.take: Internal Draft → Published status change on a curriculum module with a 'Successfully updated module' toast: in a course platform, publishing is the send and there is no external hand-off.

references.title: Adding content to Google Classroom
references.question: Q5
references.take: Complete external hand-off: Export menu lists Google Classroom next to Docs / PDF, a permission modal says what will be shared, an OAuth enable step, a Class picker maps the document to one class, and a toast confirms the export.

references.title: Community course feed with announcements
references.question: Q6
references.take: Sidebar with 'Announcements' as its own space separate from 'Feed' and a notification bell in the header, so admin announcements have a dedicated place instead of mixing into ordinary posts.

references.title: Course announcements feed with pinned posts
references.question: Q6
references.take: Teacher-posted course announcement visible to families showing rich text, imagery, likes, and comments for learner reception.

references.title: Course discussion and activity feed (iOS)
references.question: Q6
references.take: Mobile discussion list sorted by Latest that mixes a bug report, a technical question and a lecture question with no pin, unread marker or sender role: an announcement dropped here would be indistinguishable from peer chatter.

references.title: Course channel announcements and posts
references.question: Q6
references.take: Team channel announcement post with metadata showing how learners receive course updates with reply and engagement options.

references.title: Activity and announcements inbox (iOS)
references.question: Q6
references.take: Mobile notification and activity inbox showing how learners receive course announcements and mentions in centralized notification interface.

references.title: Spotify notification settings: per-category Email/Push toggles
references.question: Q6
references.take: Spotify's Notification settings list content categories (Music, Podcasts, Audiobooks, Concerts, Livestreams), each with its own Email and Push checkboxes, modeling how a learner-facing portal could let people set per-category channel preferences for course communications.
